issues.legal_issue: A withdrawal of an invalid or ineffective acquisition declaration does not exhaust the notification that preceded it.
material_facts: The lands were covered by an acquisition notification followed by a declaration.
The declaration was challenged because the affected landowners had not been heard on their objections.
The government withdrew the declaration after the procedural illegality was raised, and the landowners were then heard before a fresh declaration was issued.
issues.conclusion: The withdrawal did not make the original acquisition notification ineffective or infructuous; the notification could support a fresh declaration.
issues.legal_principle: A valid declaration under Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 exhausts the scope of the Section 4 notification. That rule does not apply where the declaration is invalid, ineffective or infructuous. There is no distinction between a declaration held invalid by a court and one withdrawn by the government after an obvious illegality is pointed out. The Court followed Girdhari Lal Amrit Lal v. State, State v. Haider Bux and State v. Bhogilal Keshavlal; distinguished State v. Vishnu Prasad Sharma; and disapproved Ajit Singh v. State.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land under a statutory acquisition process.
predicates.court_found_declaration_invalid: A court determined that the acquisition declaration was invalid or ineffective.
predicates.government_withdrew_declaration_after_ob: The government withdrew the acquisition declaration after an obvious illegality in it was pointed out.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding involves an invalid declaration, whether judicially invalidated or withdrawn by the government after an obvious illegality was raised, the original notification remains available for further acquisition proceedings.

issues.legal_issue: A later acquisition notification supersedes an earlier notification for land covered by both notifications.
material_facts: A later acquisition notification covered some, but not all, of the land covered by the earlier notification.
No declaration had been issued pursuant to the later notification when the High Court heard the matter.
issues.conclusion: For land covered by both notifications, further acquisition proceedings must proceed only under the later notification, and proceedings under the earlier notification are deemed superseded.
issues.legal_principle: Where a later acquisition notification covers land also covered by an earlier notification, the earlier notification is superseded as to that land, and further acquisition proceedings for it must be taken in accordance with law under the later notification.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the acquisition of land under a statutory acquisition process.
predicates.later_notification_covers_same_land: A later acquisition notification includes land that was also included in an earlier acquisition notification.

issues.definition: If a later notification in an acquisition proceeding includes land also included in an earlier notification, proceedings for that overlapping land proceed only under the later notification.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge alleging bad faith and failure to apply the mind to an acquisition notification may be rejected when the reviewing court finds no merit in it.
material_facts: The landowners challenged the acquisition notification on grounds of bad faith and failure to apply the mind.
The High Court rejected those grounds, and the Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with that conclusion.
issues.conclusion: The challenge to the acquisition notification on those grounds was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Supreme Court found no reason to interfere with the High Court's conclusion that the challenge based on bad faith and failure to apply the mind had no merit.

predicates.land_acquisition_notification_challenged: A party challenged a notification issued for the acquisition of land.
predicates.high_court_rejected_bad_faith_or_nonappl: The High Court rejected a challenge alleging bad faith or failure to apply the mind in issuing the notification.

issues.definition: When a land acquisition notification is challenged and the High Court has rejected the bad-faith or failure-to-apply-the-mind challenge, the challenge is rejected on appeal.
